subtasks.title: Define shared types for serve package
subtasks.description:
Create internal/serve/serve.go with foundational types needed by all other subtasks. This is a types-only foundation — no behavioral logic.

Create:
- Config struct with fields: Addr string, BearerToken string, Store StoreQuerier
- StoreQuerier interface with single method: AgentDashboard() ([]csuite.AgentDashboardRow, error) — consumption-site interface per ARCHITECTURE.md 'Interfaces at consumption sites' rule
- Server struct with fields: cfg Config, srv *http.Server
- NewServer(cfg Config) *Server constructor (trivial field assignment)

The StoreQuerier interface decouples the serve package from *csuite.Store, enabling mock-based testing. csuite.Store already satisfies this interface via its AgentDashboard() method.

Imports: only net/http and internal/csuite (for AgentDashboardRow type).

subtasks.title: Write tests for auth middleware
subtasks.description:
Create internal/serve/auth_test.go with tests for bearer token authentication middleware. Create minimal stub in internal/serve/auth.go (function signature only, returns no-op middleware) so tests compile but fail.

Test cases:
1. Valid token: request with 'Authorization: Bearer <correct-token>' passes through, inner handler is called and writes 200
2. Missing header: request with no Authorization header returns 401 with JSON {"error":"unauthorized"}
3. Wrong token: request with incorrect bearer token returns 401 with JSON {"error":"unauthorized"}
4. Malformed header: request with 'Authorization: Token xyz' (wrong prefix) returns 401
5. Empty token in config: middleware rejects all requests with 401

Use httptest.NewRecorder and httptest.NewRequest. Verify Content-Type is application/json on 401 responses.

Function signature to test: AuthMiddleware(token string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler

subtasks.title: Implement auth middleware
subtasks.description:
Implement AuthMiddleware in internal/serve/auth.go. Replace the stub from the test subtask with full implementation.

Behavior:
- Takes a bearer token string, returns standard http middleware func(http.Handler) http.Handler
- Extracts Authorization header value
- Verifies 'Bearer ' prefix (case-sensitive)
- Uses crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare for timing-safe token comparison
- On auth failure: respond with 401 status, Content-Type application/json, body {"error":"unauthorized"}
- On success: call next handler

All pre-written tests in auth_test.go must pass. Do NOT modify the test file.

subtasks.title: Write tests for handlers and server lifecycle
subtasks.description:
Create internal/serve/handlers_test.go and internal/serve/serve_test.go. Create minimal stub in internal/serve/handlers.go (function signatures returning 501) so tests compile but fail.

handlers_test.go tests:
1. GET /api/health returns 200 with JSON {"status":"ok"} and Content-Type application/json
2. GET /api/agents with mock StoreQuerier returns 200 with JSON array of agents (verify name, status, unread_count fields)
3. GET /api/agents when store returns error returns 500 with JSON {"error":"internal server error"}
4. Integration test using testutil.NewTestStore: create agents via testutil.CreateCsuiteAgent, verify GET /api/agents returns them with correct unread counts

Define a mockStore struct in handlers_test.go implementing StoreQuerier for unit tests.

serve_test.go tests:
1. NewServer creates a server with correct config
2. Server.ListenAndServe starts serving and responds to requests; Server.Shutdown stops it gracefully
3. Routes are wired correctly: /api/health is accessible, /api/agents requires auth

Use httptest for handler tests. For serve_test.go, use net.Listen on :0 for ephemeral port.

subtasks.title: Implement handlers and server lifecycle
subtasks.description:
Implement internal/serve/handlers.go and complete Server.ListenAndServe/Shutdown in internal/serve/serve.go.

handlers.go:
- HandleHealth() http.HandlerFunc: returns JSON {"status":"ok"} with 200
- HandleAgents(store StoreQuerier) http.HandlerFunc: calls store.AgentDashboard(), marshals result as JSON array. Each element has json tags for snake_case: name, status, unread_count, latest_inbox. On store error, returns 500 with {"error":"internal server error"}. Set Content-Type: application/json.

serve.go additions:
- Server.ListenAndServe() error: creates http.ServeMux, registers GET /api/health (no auth), registers GET /api/agents (behind AuthMiddleware), creates http.Server with Addr from config, calls ListenAndServe
- Server.Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error: delegates to internal http.Server.Shutdown

All pre-written tests must pass. Do NOT modify test files.

subtasks.title: Integration: serve subcommand, config, dependency, and docs
subtasks.description:
Wire the serve package into the csuite-watcher CLI and add configuration.

cmd/csuite-watcher/main.go changes:
1. Add serveTomlConfig struct: Addr string `toml:"addr"`, BearerToken string `toml:"bearer_token"`, DBPath string `toml:"db_path"` — following watcherTomlConfig pattern
2. Add Serve field to dremToml struct: Serve serveTomlConfig `toml:"serve"`
3. Add loadServeConfig function following loadWatcherConfig pattern
4. Add 'serve' case to subcommand switch in run() function
5. Implement runServe(args []string, stderr io.Writer) int: parse -config flag, load serve config, open csuite.db with gorm+sqlite, AutoMigrate CsuiteAgent and CsuiteInboxMessage, create csuite.NewStore(db), create serve.NewServer with serve.Config, run ListenAndServe in goroutine, wait for SIGTERM/SIGINT via signal.NotifyContext, call Shutdown
6. Update usage strings to include 'serve' subcommand

drem.toml changes:
- Add [serve] section with addr = ':8080', bearer_token = 'changeme', db_path = '~/.drem-csuite/csuite.db'

Dependency:
- Run `go get nhooyr.io/websocket` to add to go.mod/go.sum

Documentation:
- Add brief serve subcommand section to README.md (if it exists) or create docs/bridge-server.md with usage, config, and endpoint documentation

Verification:
- go build ./cmd/csuite-watcher
- go vet ./...
- go test ./internal/serve/... ./cmd/csuite-watcher/...
- gofmt -l ./internal/serve/ ./cmd/csuite-watcher/
- Verify file lengths under 800 lines
- Verify internal/serve imports ≤ 6 internal packages

tdd_exceptions.justification: Shared foundation subtask defining types and interfaces only — no behavioral logic. Constructor is trivial field assignment. Types are validated by downstream test subtasks that depend on them.

Integration wiring connecting already-tested serve package to existing main.go subcommand switch. Behavioral correctness verified by go build + go vet + existing serve package tests. Config parsing follows established loadWatcherConfig pattern.

assumptions.decision: Health endpoint is unauthenticated, agents endpoint requires bearer token
assumptions.why_chosen: Health endpoints are conventionally unauthenticated for load balancer probes and monitoring. Agent data contains business state and should be protected.

assumptions.decision: StoreQuerier interface at consumption site (internal/serve) rather than using *csuite.Store directly
assumptions.why_chosen: ARCHITECTURE.md constitution rule 'Interfaces at consumption sites' explicitly requires this pattern. Enables mock-based unit testing without real DB.

assumptions.decision: Using stdlib http.ServeMux for routing (not a third-party router)
assumptions.why_chosen: Only 2 routes needed. stdlib is sufficient, avoids unnecessary dependencies, and matches project's minimal dependency approach.

assumptions.decision: Server.ListenAndServe() + Server.Shutdown(ctx) as the lifecycle API
alternatives: Single Run(ctx) method that blocks until context cancellation
assumptions.why_chosen: Matches stdlib http.Server API shape. Allows the caller (main.go) to control shutdown timing with its own context, matching the runWatcher pattern.

assumptions.decision: JSON response fields use snake_case (name, status, unread_count, latest_inbox)
assumptions.why_chosen: snake_case matches the TOML config field naming convention used throughout the project and is conventional for REST APIs consumed by diverse clients.
8080 is the conventional HTTP alternative port. Binding all interfaces is standard for server processes (restrict via config if needed).

assumptions.decision: nhooyr.io/websocket added to go.mod but not used in handler code yet
alternatives: Skip dependency until websocket handlers are implemented
assumptions.why_chosen: Task description explicitly requires adding this dependency. Prepares for future websocket endpoints.

assumptions.decision: Serve subcommand opens its own DB connection rather than sharing with watcher
alternatives: Share DB connection if both run in same process
assumptions.why_chosen: serve and run are separate subcommands that run independently. Each opens its own connection following the established runWatcher pattern.
